newsitem.title: UK: Shell falls as Q1 news disappoints.
newsitem.headline: Shell falls as Q1 news disappoints.

text.p: Shares in Shell Transport and Trading Co Plc fell 9p to 1,081p, reflecting disappointment over first quarter profits and a cautious statement accompanying results, analysts said.
The shares were 3p higher before the news.
Royal Dutch/Shell Group revealed current cost before exceptional items of 1.545 billion stg against expectations of 1.355 billion to 1.736 billion.
"A lot of people were a little high with their forecasts," said an analyst.
"And there are the usual cautious mutterings about the second half with supply upstream and downstream likely to be plentiful and prices and margins under pressure - nothing new," he said.

Another analyst said key negative points were warmer weather in Europe during the period and poor Far Eastern refining and marketing margins. Shell's tax charge was up to 51 percent from 41 percent, although last year's first quarter could be viewed as the erratic figure due to tax credits in that period, he said.
Capital expenditure was down again year on year.

"The optimists would say that's positive because they're raking in lots of cash, the pessimists would say it persistently undershoots what they say they're going to spend and where's the growth going to come from," he said.
